description: Cross-binding conformance for esm-spec §6.6.3's comparison rule when the ACTUAL value of an assertion is not finite. An assertion passes only when `actual == expected` or both values are finite and within the resolved tolerance; a ±Inf or NaN actual therefore FAILS against every finite `expected`, and no tolerance can rescue it. Without the finiteness guard the tolerance arithmetic is vacuously satisfied for an infinite actual -- `|Inf - e| = Inf <= max(atol, rtol*max(Inf, |e|)) = Inf` -- so an assertion passes whatever it expected, and an overflow, a division by a zero denominator or a log(0) reports green. NaN fails on its own (every comparison with NaN is false), which is why the hole was specific to an infinity and why NaN is carried here as a control. Julia is the reference binding: its `_check_assertion` delegates to `isapprox`, which is defined as `x == y || (isfinite(x) && isfinite(y) && |x-y| <= max(atol, rtol*max(|x|,|y|)))` and already conforms. The verdicts, not the actuals, are what is compared: ±Inf and NaN are not JSON-representable, so this tier's expectations live in the manifest as a per-assertion (actual_class, passed) pair rather than in a numeric golden.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no inline-test assertion comparison
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no inline-test assertion comparison

cases.note: The defect in its plainest form: +Inf asserted to be 42.
The same cell asserted to be 0. Contradicts case 1, so at most one could ever pass.
Against the largest finite double. A magnitude test would call this close; finiteness is not a magnitude test.
abs=1e300 is the widest tolerance a document can spell, and it does not rescue an infinity: finiteness is judged BEFORE tolerance.
-Inf against a negative expected: the sign agrees and the verdict is still FAIL.
CONTROL, correct in every binding before this tier existed: NaN fails because every IEEE comparison with NaN is false.
NON-VACUITY: a finite actual equal to its expected still PASSES. A binding that failed everything would fail here.
NON-VACUITY, the other way: a finite actual far from its expected still FAILS.
